 How early can you vote in person for Michigan’s 2026 General Election? Here’s what to know
 Election Day is on Tuesday, Nov. 3.
 Samantha Sayles , Senior Digital Producer
 Published:  October 21, 2026 at 1:19 PM Updated:  October 21, 2026 at 1:57 PM Tags:  Decision 2026 , Michigan , Elections Election Day in Michigan is on Tuesday, Nov. 3, but voters can cast their ballots earlier.
 Voters can head to an early voting site to cast their ballot in person before Election Day.
 Here’s what voters need to know: 
 What is early voting?
 Early voting allows voters to cast a ballot before Election Day. During the early voting period, voters receive a ballot and can insert it directly into a tabulator at their early voting site.
 Michigan voters approved a constitutional amendment in November 2022 that gives voters the right to vote early and in person at an early voting site before statewide and federal elections. 
 When is early voting?
 Early voting in Michigan begins Michigan’s mandatory early voting period begins the second Saturday before Election Day and ends the Sunday before an election. But communities can choose to add more early voting days for those elections and can offer early voting for local elections.
 State law gives communities the option to offer early voting beginning 29 days before the election. But starting in 2026, communities can provide early voting on the Monday before Election Day.
 Early voting for the 2026 General Election will begin on Saturday, Oct. 24, for all Michigan voters.
 Where can I vote early?
 Voters can look up their assigned early voting site up to 60 days before Election Day. Click here to find your early voting site . 
 What is an early voting site?
 An early voting site is a polling place where voters can cast their ballot before Election Day, during the early voting period. Voters from more than one precinct, city or township can be assigned to a single, shared early voting site.
 How is early voting different from absentee voting?
 Early voting lets voters cast their ballots like they would at a polling place on Election Day. Voters receive a ballot and can complete it before personally placing it in the tabulator at their early voting site.
 Absentee voting gives voters a chance to request a ballot by mail, online or in person at their local clerk’s office. Voters can complete their absentee ballot at home or at their local clerk’s office and submit it by mail, in person, or via drop box. After the local clerk receives an absentee ballot, election inspectors verify it and tabulate it.
 Since 2024, absentee voters can take their completed absentee ballot to their early voting site or polling place on Election Day (except in Detroit) and place it directly into the tabulator.
 Who can vote early?
 Any registered Michigan voter can vote early in person at an early voting site for statewide and federal elections.
 Voters can register to vote up to and on Election Day, including the early voting period.
 Can I vote early if I have a disability?
 All voters have the right to vote in person at an early voting site, at a polling place, or by using a standard or accessible absentee ballot.
 Early voting sites require at least one Voter Assist Terminal (VAT). VATs can help voters with visual, hearing, mobility or other disabilities.
 Early voting sites will also offer accessible curbside voting. Voters may need to send someone into the early voting site to request curbside voting on their behalf. An election official will then bring the ballot outside for the voter to complete.
 Can I register to vote at an early voting site?
 Voters should vote at their current address before visiting an early voting site. Click here to register. 
 Within 14 days of an election, voters must visit their local clerk’s office and provide proof of residency to register.
 Early voting sites don’t offer voter registration, but if an early voting site is located at a clerk’s office or satellite office, voters can register to vote on site. 
 Are you registered to vote in Michigan? Here’s how to check ahead of November general election 
 Do I need to bring ID to vote at an early voting site?
 Voters should bring an acceptable form of photo ID to an early voting site or to the polls on Election Day, but a photo ID is not required to cast a ballot.
 Voters without a photo ID, or those who forgot to bring one, can still vote after signing an Affidavit of Voter Not in Possession of Picture Identification.
 Can I change my vote after voting early?
 You cannot change your vote once you insert the ballot into a tabulator.
 Voters who complete and submit an absent voter ballot by mail, in person at a local clerk’s office, or via drop box, have the option to change their vote by spoiling their original ballot and requesting a new one:
 The deadline for spoiling a returned absentee ballot is 5 p.m. on the second Friday before the election. 
 The deadline for spoiling an unreturned absentee ballot and receiving another by mail is the Friday immediately before the election at 5 p.m. 
 The deadline to spoil and receive another in-person absentee ballot is the day before the election at 4 p.m. 
 Voters who insert their absentee ballot into a tabulator at an early voting site cannot spoil their ballot or change their vote.
 When are early voting ballots counted?
 Election officials total and report all ballots, including those submitted at an early voting site, along with absentee ballots and Election Day ballots after polls close at 8 p.m. on Election Day.
